questions.prompt: Put the models of the atom in the order they were proposed.
questions.explain: Each model built on or replaced the one before, as new evidence appeared.

questions.prompt: Match each scientist to their discovery or idea.
questions.explain: Each scientist added a key piece to the atomic model.

questions.prompt: In the gold foil experiment, MOST alpha particles went straight through. This shows that…
options: alpha particles are very small
gold is a liquid
the atom is mostly empty space
the atom is a solid ball
questions.explain: If most particles meet nothing, most of the atom must be empty space.

questions.prompt: A very few alpha particles bounced straight back. What did this suggest?
options: Atoms are made of pudding
The foil was too thick
There is a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus
Electrons are very heavy
questions.explain: Only a tiny, heavy, positive centre could turn a fast positive particle all the way round.

questions.prompt: What did Thomson's plum pudding model look like?
options: A solid sphere with nothing inside
Negative electrons dotted through a ball of positive charge
A tiny nucleus with electrons in shells
A cube of protons
questions.explain: Like plums (electrons) in a pudding (positive charge).

questions.text: The ancient Indian philosopher ___ called the smallest particles of matter ___.
questions.explain: Maharishi Kanad described paramanu over 2,000 years ago.

questions.prompt: Why was the plum pudding model replaced?
options: It was too simple to draw
Rutherford didn't like puddings
New experimental evidence (gold foil results) could not be explained by it
Thomson was a careless scientist
questions.explain: Models are replaced when new evidence doesn't fit. That's how science progresses.

questions.prompt: Which were parts of Dalton's atomic theory? Choose all that apply.
options: All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms
Atoms of the same element are identical
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds
Atoms contain electrons
Atoms have a tiny nucleus
questions.explain: Electrons (1897) and the nucleus (1911) were discovered after Dalton.

questions.prompt: Describe the three main observations of Rutherford's gold foil experiment and what each one showed.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Most alpha particles passed straight through, so the atom is mostly empty space. 2) Some were deflected by small angles, so there is a positive charge that repels them. 3) Very few bounced back, so the positive charge and most of the mass is concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.
rubric: Most went through → mostly empty space
Very few bounced back → tiny, dense nucleus
questions.explain: Each observation leads to one conclusion. Link them clearly.
